title: Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook

blocks.text: The Internet & SaaS Access Control Policies Support Troubleshooting Runbook provides comprehensive guidance for troubleshooting requests related to scenarios involving URL, domain, IP address, file analysis, and related vulnerabilities. It highlights various checks on third-party websites and Zscaler's tools that help you achieve clarity on the security verdicts. By following these structured steps, users can efficiently address issues related to Zscaler's access control policies and ensure proper handling of security threats.
The following section describes the triage process for access control policies.

blocks.item: Does the website load after a delay or not at all?
Delay or slowness: Issues with Internet & SaaS performance.
Other cases: Continue.
Do transactions go through Zscaler?
No or Not sure: Traffic does not go through Zscaler.
Other cases: Continue.
Is the website using Quick UDP Internet Connections (QUIC)?

I don't know: What is QUIC? QUIC, also known as http/3 or simply h3, is a transport protocol developed by Google that improves the performance of connection-oriented web applications. It operates over User Datagram Protocol (UDP) instead of TCP and integrates features like connection migration, multiplexing without head-of-line blocking, and built-in encryption (TLS 1.3).

Key benefits of QUIC include reduced latency due to faster connection establishment (0-RTT and 1-RTT handshakes), improved congestion control, and resilience to packet loss. It's widely used in http/3, where it enhances web performance by eliminating many inefficiencies associated with traditional TCP-based protocols.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Managing the QUIC Protocol.
To determine if a website is using QUIC, see How to Determine if a Website is Using QUIC.
These issues can be broadly classified into the three categories, described in the following sections. Follow the symptoms that are the closest match to your case.
If you want to know if your policy configuration is correct or if a resource is correctly categorized by Zscaler.

blocks.item: URL Filtering: Resolve user-defined URL category conflicts.
SSL Inspection: Add Zscaler's certificate to a specific application's certificate store.
Cloud App: Cloud app instance, tenant profile / tenancy restriction.
URL Filtering / Cloud App: Look up the URL Category and Cloud App for a given URL.

blocks.text: The policy is correctly configured but the web or firewall logs show a contradicting policy action.

blocks.item: The Allow policy is configured but access gets blocked or cautioned as confirmed by the web logs. Look at the Policy Action field's value for the concerned URL and click one of the following:
Undecryptable Traffic Block
Not Allowed to Use HTTP Tunnel
Blocked Due to Server Probe Failure
Access Denied Due to Bad Server Certificate
Blocked Due to Bad SSL Record
Access Denied Due to Domain Fronting
Not Allowed to Browse this Category
Other reasons: Submit a case to Zscaler Support containing the information mentioned in Initial Information Set.

SSL Inspection: There are no exemptions in SSL Inspection policy but traffic does not get inspected as confirmed by the web logs. Look at the SSL Policy Reason field's value for the concerned URL and refer to the SSL Policy Reason Runbook.
SSL Inspection: Untrusted Server Certificate Gets Allowed
SSL Inspection: Inspected Despite Do Not Inspect Action in the Policy
Cloud App: Block Action is Configured for One Activity but All Activities Get Allowed as Confirmed by the Web Logs
Firewall Control:
Allow Due to Insufficient App Data
Bypassed Due to Missing Config
Specific Criteria in the Access Control Policy are not Correctly Matching the Transactions
Other issues where the web logs confirm that the policy is not working as expected: Submit a case to Zscaler Support containing the information mentioned in Initial Information Set.

blocks.text: None of the earlier options apply to your case.

blocks.item: Unable to Access Specific Websites or Web Applications
Block Policy Configured but Access Gets Allowed

blocks.text: Zscaler Support recommends that you enable Remote Assistance in view-only mode. Additionally, provide the following information:

blocks.item: Client IP from the impacted end user's system (output of ipconfig /all and route print 165.225.* from a command prompt on a Windows PC and output of ifconfig /all and route get 165.225.0.0 from a terminal on a Mac system).
A screenshot of the complete page at https://ip.zscaler.com.
A screenshot of the error message seen in the web browser or the application, if applicable.
The timestamp or period during which this access was attempted.
Complete URL or Destination IP of the application.
Policy Name or a screenshot of the relevant policy.

blocks.text: Alternatively, if remote assistance cannot be enabled, download the Web Insights logs containing all the columns for the corresponding period. It's best to use not more than 2–3 relevant filters to optimize the number of logs in the exported file while still retaining a wide enough context for analysis. Some useful filters: URL Search, User, Client IP, Location.
